method: Actual bundled Three.js PerspectiveCamera, matrices and Vector3.project; actual scene.js update/aim and core collision/raycast. Only WebGLRenderer is mocked. Real app pointer listener harness verifies logical yaw/pitch deltas. CSS rotation represented by logical viewport and inverse-mapped physical pointer events.
limitations: Not browser or physical device rendering; collision fixtures are deliberately placed behind the player
Screen-left means logical game viewport left, which rotates with the game layout
Does not assert every character vertex remains onscreen at close walls

checks.name: Character head and torso remain left of center across all views
Actual scene camera raycast stays on center reticle
Wall collision shortens camera distance without changing left shoulder
Camera rendering does not mutate gameplay yaw
Bunker hides player model and removes shoulder camera offset
Existing touch assistance still selects a visible near-center target
checks.note: Existing assist may choose an enemy off the exact screen center; the initial aiming ray itself remains centered.

checks.name: Logical drag yaw/pitch feel is unchanged in every display orientation
